judge.summary: The patient requested an appointment with Dr. Chen on Tuesday, then interrupted the agent to switch to Thursday. The agent successfully pivoted to the new request, corrected the provider specialty information, and confirmed the appointment for Thursday at 9:00 AM with Dr. Chen. The agent maintained the patient's details throughout the interaction.

conversation_quality.notes: The agent handled the interruption well, though the agent's explanation of provider specialties was slightly confusing (initially saying Dr. Reed handles ankles, then saying Dr. Chen handles knees/hips/ankles).

agent_quality.notes: The agent was slightly contradictory regarding which doctor handles ankle injuries, but successfully booked the requested slot.

technical_quality.notes: There was a 3-second dead air period noted in the metrics, which slightly impacted the pacing.

candidate_issues.title: Conflicting provider specialty information
candidate_issues.quote: Dr. Chen specializes in knees and hips, so we would typically schedule an ankle injury with Dr. Reed.
candidate_issues.why_it_matters: It creates confusion for the patient regarding which doctor is appropriate for their injury.

criteria.criterion: The agent stops when interrupted and answers the interrupting question instead of finishing its script
criteria.evidence: 00:21-00:22: Patient interrupts, agent immediately acknowledges the switch to Thursday.

criteria.criterion: The final booking reflects the latest request (Thursday, any doctor), not the earlier Tuesday / Doctor Chen ask
criteria.evidence: 00:33: 'Got you down for Thursday at 9:00 AM with Dr. Chen.'

criteria.criterion: Details already given (name, DOB, reason) are not asked for again after an interruption
criteria.evidence: The agent did not re-ask for name, DOB, or reason after the interruption.

criteria.criterion: Day, time and doctor are stated back clearly at the end

hypotheses.hypothesis: Agent offers or books a slot that violates a time-of-day, weekday or provider constraint the caller stated, and does not acknowledge the constraint
Agent talks over the interruption or resumes its previous sentence as if nothing happened
Agent books Tuesday (the first request) or keeps offering Doctor Chen after the patient dropped that preference
Agent loses collected details after a barge-in and re-asks for name and DOB from the top
Agent ends up confirming two appointments (Tuesday and Thursday) without cancelling one

positive_controls: Agent successfully handled the barge-in at 00:21
Agent correctly retained patient identity and reason throughout the call
simulator_notes: The simulator performed well in testing the barge-in capability.
judge.testing_value: This scenario effectively tested the agent's ability to handle interruptions and maintain state, which is critical for a natural receptionist experience.
